title: Daniel Frayne notes the gaps at Muileann òg
summary: A wool-buyer at the Moot's own table tells Daniel Frayne that the fair at Muileann òg now stands with gaps between its tents where none stood before, the fair's own wardens filling them each year with a wider aisle rather than own that the crowd has thinned.

title: The old die broken at Cathair dhearg
summary: With Mairead crowned, the die that struck Eòghan's own likeness on the realm-coin is broken at Cathair dhearg by the mint's custom, the old coin kept good until the new is struck in number enough to answer for it.

title: Daniel Frayne binds primers for Muileann shean
summary: Asked for primers by Muileann shean's own maor, Daniel Frayne binds forty copies of a reading-book at his own bench at Muileann leathan and sends them north on the first cart with room, the forms unchanged since he first set the type twenty years before.

title: Muileann shean's benches pass thirty
summary: The school Muileann shean opened for hewers' children the Guild will not bind grows within the year from eleven pupils to above thirty, though three of the first eleven have already gone south to hire themselves out as chain-hands in the ports.

title: The first bolt off the Doire ghlas looms
summary: The wool mills raised at Doire ghlas with the Moot's own coin turn their first bolt, a grey twill with a white thread at the selvedge, and the overseer writes to Caol mhòr that it is better cloth than the south's own factors reckoned a northern loom could turn out.

title: The Rail Board refuses the first wagon
summary: The Rail Board's factors at Muileann leathan refuse to carry the Doire ghlas mill's first wagon-load south to Muileann òg, giving no reason beyond the Board's own long custom of judging for itself what the line will carry.

title: The Moot brings its suit to Seann Bhral
summary: Daniel Frayne rides west to the circuit court at Seann Bhral with the mill's ledgers and the Board's letter of refusal, asking Ruairidh mac Phàdraig to rule whether a carrier chartered by the Crown may refuse one people's cargo and take another's.

title: Word of Catrìona nic Neacail's going
summary: A Board clerk's notice of the Mac Ùisdein sale reaches Caol mhòr with a passing word that the surveyor who drew the search's last sheet has resigned her post to teach at Caol shean, a name Daniel Frayne knows only at second hand.

title: The first Doire ghlas bale rides the coal line
summary: A year after the ruling, the Rail Board's own factor at Muileann leathan weighs the first Doire ghlas bale onto the wagon without comment, the same weight given any cargo that pays the rate, and Daniel Frayne rides down to see it loaded.
